column2: The mind alone is intention; the mind alone is the individual; the mind alone is thought, and the mind alone is ego.
The mind alone is great bondage; the mind is the inner instrument; the mind alone is earth; the mind alone is water.
The mind alone is fire; the mind alone is the great wind; the mind alone is space; the mind alone is sound.
Touch, form, taste, smell, the five sheaths are born of the mind; waking, dream, deep sleep and the rest are said to be made of mind.
The guardians of the quarters, Vasus, Rudras and Adityas are made of mind; the seen, the dull, the pairs of opposites, ignorance, are held to be mental.
Whatever is mere intention — be certain it does not exist. The whole world does not exist, does not exist; teacher and disciple and the rest do not exist — thus the Upanishad.
Ribhu said: Know all as being-consciousness; all is spread out as being-consciousness; being-consciousness-bliss, non-dual; being-consciousness-bliss, without a second.
Mere being-consciousness-bliss, being-consciousness-bliss and nothing else; I am of the form of being-consciousness-bliss; space itself is being-consciousness-bliss.
You are being-consciousness-bliss alone; I am being-consciousness-bliss; these combinations of mind, intellect, ego and thought —
not you, not I, nor anything else: all is only Brahman alone. No sentence, no word, no Veda, no syllable, nothing dull anywhere.
Neither middle, nor beginning, nor end; neither truth nor born of bondage; neither sorrow nor pleasure nor state; neither illusion nor nature.
No body, no face, no nose, no tongue, no palate; no teeth, lips, forehead, nor inhalation and exhalation.
No sweat, bone, flesh, no blood, no urine; no far, no near, no limb, no belly, no crown.
No moving of hands and feet, no scripture, no command; no knower, knowing or known; no waking, dream or sleep.
Nothing of mine is beyond the Fourth; all is spread as being-consciousness. Not the individual, not the elemental, not the divine, not the illusory.
Not Vishva, Taijasa, Prajna; not Virat, Sutra, Ishvara; no striving of coming and going, no loss, no purpose.
No abandonment, no grasping, no fault; no impure or pure; not fat, not thin, not wet; not time, not speech of place.
Not all, not fear, not duality; not trees, grasses or mountains; not meditation, nor accomplishment of yoga; not Brahmin, Vaishya or Kshatriya.
No bird, no beast, no embodied, no greed, no delusion; no pride, no envy, no desire, anger and the rest.
No woman, Shudra, cat and so on; no food or what is eaten; no mature or lacking, no atheism, no occasion for talk.
No worldly, no world, no business, no foolishness; no enjoyer, meal or food; no vessel, drink or drinkable.
No enemy, friend, son and so on; no mother, father, sister; no birth, death, growth; no delusion "I am the body."
Neither void nor non-void; not the cycle of the inner instrument; no night, no day, no evening; no Brahma, Hari, Shiva.
No weekday, fortnight, month and the like, nor year, nor flickering; no Brahmaloka, Vaikuntha, Kailasa or other.
No heaven, no Indra; no world of fire, nor Agni; no Yama or world of Yama; no worlds or guardians of worlds.
No Bhur, Bhuvah, Svah, the three worlds; no underworld or earth; neither ignorance nor knowledge; no dull illusion or nature.
No steady, no momentary, no destruction; no going, no running; nothing to be meditated on, no meditation of mine, no mantra, no repetition anywhere.
No objects, no one worthy of worship, no anointing, no worship; no flower, fruit, leaf, perfume, incense.
No hymn, no salutation, not even an atom of circumambulation; no prayer, no separateness, no oblation, no salutation to fire.
No oblation, no rites; no ill speech or good speech; no Gayatri, no twilight; no mind-state, no ill-state.
No bad hope, no wicked soul, no Chandala, no Pulkasa; no unbearable, no ill talk, no Kirata, no deceit.
No partiality or party; no ornament or thief; no pride or proud; no low or high man.
Not one, two, three, four; no greatness, no smallness; not full, not limited; no Kashi, no vow, no austerity.
No lineage, family, thread; no all-pervasiveness, no emptiness; no woman, no girl, no old woman, no maiden, no lack of thread.
No impurity of birth or death; no turning inward and illusion; no great saying, no unity, no powers like anima.
Because all is mere consciousness, there is never any fault; all is of the form of mere being, mere being-consciousness-bliss.
Brahman alone is all; there is no other; I am that, I am that likewise; I am that alone, that alone; I am Brahman, the eternal.
I am Brahman, not a worldly being; I am Brahman, not mind; I am Brahman, not intellect; I am Brahman, not senses.
I am Brahman, not body; I am Brahman, not an object; I am Brahman, not an individual; I am Brahman, not a ground of difference.
I am Brahman, not dull; I am Brahman, I have no death; I am Brahman, not breath; I am Brahman, higher than the highest.
This is Brahman, supreme Brahman, true Brahman, the lord; time is Brahman, art is Brahman, happiness is Brahman, self-luminous.
One is Brahman, two are Brahman; delusion is Brahman, and peace and the rest; fault is Brahman, quality is Brahman; self-control, peace, the all-pervading, the lord.
The world is Brahman, the teacher is Brahman, the disciple is Brahman, Sadashiva; the earlier is Brahman, the supreme is Brahman, the pure is Brahman, the good and bad.
The individual is always Brahman; I am being-consciousness-bliss. All is said to be made of Brahman; the world is all made of Brahman.
Brahman itself — no doubt; nothing exists apart from oneself; all is the Self, the pure Self; all is non-dual mere consciousness.
The Self of eternal stainless form; nothing is apart from the Self; this world is a shining form only of an atom's size.
The body is only atom-sized; the unreal is atom-sized; the inconceivable or the conceivable is atom-sized.
Brahman alone is all, mere consciousness; the three worlds are Brahman only; bliss, supreme bliss — nothing else at all.
Mere consciousness is Om; Brahman itself is all; I alone am all the world; I alone am the supreme state.
I alone am beyond the qualities; I alone am higher than the highest; I alone am supreme Brahman; I alone am the teacher of teachers.
I alone am the support of all; I alone am the happiness of happiness; there is no world apart from the Self; no happiness apart from the Self.
There is no goal apart from the Self; the whole world is made of the Self; nothing anywhere is apart from the Self; no grass is apart from the Self.
There is no husk apart from the Self; the whole world is made of the Self; all this is Brahman only; the unreal is not Brahman only.
All that is heard is Brahman only; oneself is Brahman alone; all that is chosen is Brahman only; the savor, the happiness is Brahman only.
Only Brahman is the space of consciousness, the imperishable being-consciousness-bliss; nothing is other than Brahman; no world is other than Brahman.
Nothing exists apart from Brahman; no fruit is apart from Brahman; no grass is apart from Brahman; no state is apart from Brahman.
No teacher is apart from Brahman; no body is apart from Brahman, unreal; no egoism is apart from Brahman; "you" and "this" are nowhere.
Know yourself as Brahman-natured; nothing is apart from oneself. Whatever is seen in the world, whatever is spoken by people,
whatever is enjoyed anywhere, all that is unreal indeed. The difference of doer, of action, of quality, of taste and the like,
this difference of gender — all this is only unreal; always happiness. Difference of time, of place, of thing, victory and defeat —
whatever is difference, all that is only unreal. The inner instrument is unreal; the senses and the rest are only unreal;
the breath and the rest are all unreal; the aggregate is of unreal nature; the five sheaths so called are unreal; the five deities are unreal;
the six modifications and the like are unreal; the group of six enemies is unreal; the six seasons are unreal; likewise the six tastes are unreal.
I am mere being-consciousness-bliss; this world has not arisen. I am the Self alone, the supreme truth; no other views of the world.
I am of the form of true bliss, a body of consciousness and bliss; I alone am supreme bliss; I alone am higher than the highest.
All this is of the form of knowledge; I am knowledge-bliss, non-dual; I am of the form of light of all; I am of the form of the absence of all.
I alone ever shine — such a form is unreal from anywhere; "you" — thus supreme Brahman, of the form of consciousness and bliss.
Form of consciousness, space of consciousness, consciousness alone is supreme happiness; I am the Self alone, not unreal; I am the immovable witness, the supreme teacher.
I am mere being-consciousness-bliss; this world has not arisen. There is no time; there is no world; no illusion or nature at all.
I alone am Hari in person; I alone am Sadashiva; I am of the state of pure consciousness; of the experience of pure sattva.
I am mere non-dual bliss; I am a mass of consciousness of one savor. All is Brahman always; all is Brahman only.
All is Brahman always; all is Brahman, conscious. I am of the form of the inner controller of all, marked by being the witness of all.
The Supreme Self, the supreme light, the supreme abode, the supreme goal; I am the essence of all Vedanta, well determined by all scriptures.
I am of the nature of the bliss of yoga, the great rise of principal bliss; I am the light of all knowledge, a body of principal wisdom.
I am the light of the Fourth of the Fourth, free of the Fourth of the Fourth and the rest; I am the imperishable consciousness, truth; I am Vasudeva, ageless, deathless.
I am Brahman, the space of consciousness, eternal Brahman, stainless; pure, awake, ever free, nameless, formless.
I am of the form of being-consciousness-bliss; this world has not arisen. The true and false world does not exist; nor intention, imagining and the like.
Brahman is made of eternal bliss, alone, always by itself; infinite, imperishable, peaceful, of one form, free of disease.
If anything exists apart from me, it is false, like a mirage in a desert. If there were any fear from the words of a barren woman's son —
If a king of elephants were killed by a hare's horn, then the world would exist. If one drinking mirage-water were satisfied, let this world be.
If anyone were destroyed by a man's horn, then this indeed exists. If the city of Gandharvas were true, the world would always be.
If the blueness of the sky were true, the world would be true. If the silver in a shell were true as ornament, the world would be.
If a man bitten by a rope-snake were to be so, let there be the world; if by a golden arrow the flaming fire were destroyed, the world would be.
If there were rice-pudding in the Vindhya forest, the world would arise; if by a plantain trunk as fuel cooking succeeded, the world would be.
If cooking succeeded by the forms of newly born girls, the world would be; if darkness were destroyed by lamps in a picture, let this world be.
If a mortal dead a month ago came back, the world would be; if buttermilk were of the nature of milk anywhere, the world would be eternal.
If milk from a cow's udder could be re-planted, the world; if earth-dust arose in the ocean, let the world always be.
If an elephant in rut were bound by a tortoise's hair, let there be the world; if Meru were moved by a lotus fiber, the world would be.
If the ocean were bound by a garland of waves, let this world be; if fire were below fire, let the world always be.
If a flame were cold, this form of world would exist; if a lotus grew in a circle of flaming fire, let there be the world.
If a great mountain-king of sapphire could arise, this world would be; if Meru came and stood in a lotus bud, let this world be.
If the bee's child swallowed Meru, let this be movable; if a lion were killed by a mosquito, then let the world be true for you.
If the three worlds fit in the hollow of an atom, the world would be; if a grass fire were eternal, that world would be momentary.
If what is seen in a dream occurred in waking, the world would be; if a river's current were unmoving, by someone this world would be.
If fire were food for the hungry, then a moment would be imagined; if the blind from birth knew the nature of jewels well, the world would be always.
If a eunuch youth enjoyed a woman's pleasure, the world would be; if a chariot were built from a hare's horn, that world exists.
If a girl newly born were fit for enjoyment, the world would be; if a barren woman knew the happiness of pregnancy, let this world be.
If a crow walked like a swan, let the world be steady; if a great ass fought with a lion, then the world's continuance would hold.
If a great ass went with an elephant's gait, then let there be the world; if the full moon and sun were themselves dull, let the world shine.
If Rahu were seen leaving the moon and sun and the like, the world; if growth arose from a roasted seed, let the world be real.
